review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions of spaceGrad and spaceTimeGradNormSq. I searched the library for simp-tagged lemmas about spaceGrad, spaceTimeGradNormSq and iterateSpatialWord, and found none. I also searched for other places that re-prove the vanishing of spaceGrad on constants and the uses of iterateSpatialWord_zero. I did not run Lean, so I did not check how a new simp lemma would interact with the existing simp set. The risk looks low: the left-hand sides are specific (constant functions), so I see no loop. The nlinarith and positivity parts of the proof are outside the simp-interface rubric.

findings.problem: No canonical simp lemma says that spaceGrad of a constant (in particular zero) function is zero. So hz has to unfold the definition (`unfold spaceGrad; simp`), and hzero needs a manual `simp_rw [hzpoint]` before `simp [vecNormSq, vecDot]`. The same fact is re-proved by hand in many other places: `simp [spaceGrad]` in MeanZeroEnergy, SpaceErgodic, BracketFF and MatrixContinuity, and local `hzero`/`hzeroGrad`/`hgrad0` haves in VelocitySpatial, ChiMKCorrector and BoundedParabolicUniqueness. Each such proof unfolds the definition, which exposes `fderiv` and `basisVec`.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definition of spaceGrad, add `@[simp] theorem spaceGrad_const (c : ℝ) : spaceGrad (fun _ : Vec 2 => c) = 0`. Its proof would be `funext x i; simp [spaceGrad]`. Also add a zero case, `spaceGrad_zero`, if the form `fun _ => 0` does not match. Then hz would reduce to `simp [iterateSpatialWord_zero]` with no `unfold spaceGrad`, and hzero would be `simp [vecNormSq, vecDot]` or similar. The repeated local `hzero` lemmas elsewhere could also be dropped.
findings.benefit: Callers get the normal form `spaceGrad (const) = 0` from plain `simp`, without unfolding spaceGrad. About a dozen duplicated ad-hoc proofs can be shortened. The rewrite is safe: the left-hand side is a specific constant-function pattern and the right-hand side is simpler, so I see no loop.

evidence.excerpt: fun x i => fderiv ℝ f x (basisVec i)
have hzero : AVenhance.spaceGrad (fun _ : Vec 2 => (0 : ℝ)) = 0 := by
have hgradOne : spaceGrad (fun _ : Vec 2 => (1 : ℝ)) = 0 := by
have hgrad0 : spaceGrad (fun _ : Vec 2 => (0 : ℝ)) x i = 0 := by

findings.problem: The lemma `iterateSpatialWord_zero` (`iterateSpatialWord w (fun _ => 0) = fun _ => 0`) is not tagged `@[simp]`. Every use passes it by name to `simp only [...]` or `simpa only [...]`: here, in IteratesWordFluxTimeEnergy and in IteratesScalarMaterialEnergy. Because of this, the surrounding proofs have to use `simp only` and spell out the other lemmas, and plain `simp` cannot see through iterated spatial words of zero data. The lemma is a canonical normal-form rewrite: the right-hand side is strictly simpler, and the left-hand side is a specific pattern with zero data.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `iterateSpatialWord_zero` with `@[simp]` where it is declared in IteratesWordTimeEnergy.lean. Together with a simp lemma for spaceGrad of a constant, this lets `ext z j; simp` replace the current two-step `simp only [iterateSpatialWord_zero]; unfold spaceGrad; simp`.
findings.benefit: The zero-data collapse becomes automatic for plain `simp`, so downstream proofs about zero initial data no longer need to list the lemma. The simp set also stays consistent with the other zero lemmas used with it, such as `Pi.zero_apply`.

evidence.excerpt: simpa only [iterateSpatialWord_zero, Pi.zero_apply, zero_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, zero_add] using he
